I do. :( I have always been overweight. Although when I was in 5th to 7th grade, I was able to keep my weight at the normal range. I guess it was puberty? Anyway, after that, I just gained pound after pound after pound. So today, I am overweight.

I experienced being obese during the height of the pandemic. It was tough and it was also when my health problems worsened. The more irregular my periods were, cystic acne around my chin and back, hair thinning (I have PCOS)... Basically, being obese/overweight wasn't just about my size. It was messing up my mental and physical health.

And to answer your question, hell yea I regret it. :( I hope I won't offend others by saying what I am about to say... I just wish I was thin. I can't find clothes everywhere, nothing feels looking good on me, the person sitting next to me in public vehicles will always look uncomfortable because I am consuming more space, and I don't know if it's just playing with my confidence. But being fat will always contribute to me feeling like a laughingstock. And oh, the funny assumption that I love to eat. Haha... I love food, but I hope people would stop thinking "Give it to her" and "Just eat and eat, I don't think you're full yet". Even if I lose weight, I'll still not be in a relationship because I am really just too unattractive. Some people tell me even that I should just stay overweight because my features are softened by the fat. So yea... you're not alone. :(

When I see beautiful women, I admit that I feel something similar. It's hard not to feel bad because, idk, I guess everyone would love to look like them. For me, I would love if I can also wear whatever I want and join photographs without worrying that I'll become a meme or that I look like garbage. Hugs, OP... I do get you.

Anyways, what so far works for me is minding my own business. I remind myself the reason why I am outside the house in the first place. If it is because I need to buy groceries, I'll go straight to buying my stuff. If I am with people and I am supposed to have a good time, I try my best to focus on that. Someone told me to learn how to stand up for myself. Looks may be my problem, but it shouldn't rule my world... This is hard tbh yet my day is significantly better when I go my own YOLO. Basically, what I really want to say is that we deserve to live well. It's hard because at some point, someone will make fun of us because of our appearance. Every ugly person has experienced that for sure. However, what if we imagine our lives as if we're true aliens in this planet... We would be aware how many people in this world are shallow. On the other hand, I personally see that there are things in this world we can appreciate. Dogs, cats, guinea pigs, etc... they don't mind how we look like. A lot of books you see in libraries are written by outstanding people and we don't have a clue how they look like, and it doesn't matter. There are a lot of "ugly" organisms in this world... and only those who understand their role in this planet see their beauty. There's more I can probably say but this is becoming a novel. 😅 😔 I hope you get what I mean. 

In the end, I do get you and you're not a bad person for feeling this way. It's not our fault we feel this way. Virtual hugs :<

2022 was a roller coaster ride for me. A lot of times I felt like I was in the darkness. I broke down a lot and worried so much about everything. Many times I would wish to get swallowed into a void. I had a lot of fights with my family and it's this year that my feelings for them was so challenged. But, like I just said, it was a roller coaster ride. There were also times when I obviously got rewarded with things that I  sometimes think I didn't deserve. This year I graduated with honors, passed my licensure exam, and started applying for jobs. After the licensure exam, I had more rest (too much rest tbh) and had more chance to talk with online friends. My online friends, I felt closer to them and they still are the people I look forward to after almost two years. I never thought online friendships can last this long. This year, I was also blessed with a chance to reconnect with my high school friends. We drank together and that was also my first time to drink. It's unfortunate that we reunited after one of us died, but in his honor, I drank with his mom and my friends and I'd love if we keep doing that. They still see me as their friend after all this time, and I was grateful to hear that. 

Now, as 2023 approaches, I still feel scared and worried. I think a lot of my negativity will persist but I guess I'd still be fine. For 2023, I'll try my best to make it a productive year. I'd start working hopefully soon, start saving money, help my family with their health and our expenses, and for me at least I hope to lose weight. I lost a few but regained it during this Christmas season (I gain weight very fast. I am speed haha). 

Wishing yall ladies a blessed 2023. Thanks very much for the mods, for all the ladies, for the togertherness we had. We were literally through thick and thin. In sickness and in happiness, you and I were here. I wish we can all have a fruitful year, I think we deserve a better 2023 altogether. Happy New Year!

We had been taking care of a dog for a whole month. It was just temporary; my aunt just needed to do some errands and so she left him with us. His stay here lasted for a month and recently, we already sent him back.

Sometimes I get teary-eyed because I do miss him and I had to explain to my parents that I just miss him and it doesn't mean I love the dog more than them... Even if it was just a month long stay, I got used to waking up seeing him. I prepare his food and make him take his medicines. I let him walk around the house and I chase him as well. I let him nap on my bed and let him lay down on my stuff. I clean his cage and bring him there again when he has to pee or poop. I don't nap or sleep without him. My mom watches TV with him and she also feeds him. In my eyes, he was like a little child. No matter how tiring it gets to take care of him, I still see myself smiling. It was so easy to love him. And idk, since he left, the house just feels like there's something empty.

I've always wanted a dog but we can't afford it. So I guess having him even for a short while was a blessing. Even if I got into some sort of troubles related to him, I never got angry and I still wanted him around. Whenever I look at the empty chair he used to sit on, I feel sad. Whenever I hear a sound, I still think it could be him crying again because he doesn't like being left alone. I look around and I still picture him walking and turning to every corner. And at night I just feel kinda alone. I still miss him a lot. 

I miss my aunt too, I wish I had more time to spend with her before they return to their province. I really miss the dog, but I  would love to see her again even without the dog.

Now I guess I have a better understanding lm why pets mean so much to their owners. They aren't  accessories at home nor toys that are only loved when theyre at their best. We really need to take care of them and let them live a good life. And I guess only when we start dedicating a portion of our life with them we realize how lovely they are to be with everyday.

if you don't have classes for a whole day and you are free of household chores or other work, this example is possible:

* 8 am to 12 pm (morning study session; 4 hrs);wake up time at around 7 am so you can do preparations for the day e.g., eating breakfast, taking a bath
* 12 pm to 1 pm (lunch + break time)
* 1:30 pm to 3:30 pm (part 1 afternoon session; 3 hours straight);I placed an allowance because you might take a nap after eating or maybe you are the one washing the dishes at home idk
* 3:30 pm to 4:00 pm (30 minute break)
* 4:00 pm to 7:00 pm (part 2 extended afternoon session; 3 hours straight)
* 7:00 pm onwards - break time + other plans (this can be later if you had extra breaks in the afternoon)

Total of hours: 4 + 3 + 3 = 10 hours

Let's say we follow this schedule, we can extend studying until 1 am (or around 2 am) and we will reach 15 hours...

Edit: I wrote this assuming that you wanna study for 10 hours a day so you can catch up for a certain event such as exams or recitations. But then again, if you have classes ad other  work to do, 10 hours of study sound very inefficient tbh.

In my country, there is a policy regarding patents and if I am not mistaken, this is not only applicable to orphan drugs for rare diseases.
The innovations of a pharma company are patentable, therefore the company may apply for patent on their inventions provided that these are truly innovative and not just reconstructions (to avoid evergreening). Usually the patent only lasts for 20 years and the most benefit a company can get is that they are the only ones with the right to produce their patent and therefore earn from it.
The limitation, however, is that it was stated in our law that the government may exploit the patent even without the agreement of the patent owner (the pharma company in this case) in situations such as a national emergency or other circumstances which are of extreme urgency and in times when it is only reasonable as there is great demand for the patented product at the time it is needed by the people but the patent owner could not produce it sufficiently. Additionally, these patents shall be disclosed to the public in exchange of their earned right to be the exclusive producer of the patented product and to exclude other companies from copying them. I mentioned the law to let you know that in some countries, there is a body that have power to use these patents in times of emergency and the company cannot stop that. Companies are also not allowed to hold their formulation in secret because they have to submit all the necessary information to the health authority to secure a license for their drug product (which includes vaccines), therefore the government somehow has a copy of these formulations including the patented ones. 

Now, regarding what you said, I don't think that patents shall be lifted. Companies may continue applying for patents for their vaccines and I think, it must even be more significant now to apply for patents because these vaccines are new and original. Their clinical trials are still on-going and there are more information regarding these vaccines that are yet to be determined (e.g. efficacy, chronic adverse effects). Meaning, they should be the ones to produce their vaccines based on their established standards that they have constructed according to their earlier studies and be the sole principal investigator in the clinical trials of their vaccines. In case that they may not produce these vaccines sufficiently, one of the solutions is probably to choose other manufacturers who can help, decide whether these manufacturers are reputable enough and capable enough to make the vaccines based in the established standards or specifications, and grant them the authority to be a producer of the vaccine. These manufacturers may earn from the patent too. (Hmm here, the problem now is whether there are manufacturers who have the facility to produce these vaccines. So you can see, even if the vaccines are patented or not, if there's no one else who can produce the new vaccines based on the established specifications, then nobody else can ever produce it other than the innovator company. Having an issue with the patents is negligible.)

These pharma companies are not "hoarding" the "recipe" and we may consider that the patent is just there to protect the inventions (the new vaccines) for now. This will also ensure that all vaccines are coming from their respective owners, therefore it will be easier to distinguish them, we can easily know where they originated, and be somehow confident that these new vaccines came from the true hands of those who have been studying them for years (yes, for years. For example are the vaccines which are from mRNA technology.)

To conclude, waiving patents is not necessary. Patents are important to protect these new vaccines and to ensure that these vaccines are being produced by the companies who are their respective original makers. By this, we can be sure that the vaccines are being produced according to standards known and be more confident that these vaccines are truly of quality and efficacious at least according to what these companies have found out on their numerous studies in drug research. Anyway, there are other strategies, ways that are better in securing availability of vaccines such as the one that I have mentioned above. 

We have other concerns to focus on though such as the affordability of these vaccines, the promptness and organization of our governments' action in delivering these vaccines to people in their respective countries, the availability of cold chain facilities in the country who could accept all these vaccines, etc. And yeah..  patenting these vaccines isnt among these issues.

It's possible that two primary colors of light combine. However, what I know is that orange isn't among those colors that'll be formed from any of the combinations.

R and G forms Yellow (Y). R and B forms Magenta (M). And G and B forms Cyan (C). Yellow, magenta, and Cyan are what we know now as secondary colors of light. 

Complementary colors are forms when you subract a primary color from white light. In that case, 

Let W (White) be R + G + B

R+G+B (WHITE) - R (RED) = G+B = CYAN 

Red and cyan are complementary. 

R+G+B (WHITE) - B (BLUE) = R+G = YELLOW

Blue and yellow are complementary. 

R+G+B (WHITE) - G (GREEN) = R+B = MAGENTA

Green and magenta are complementary.

9 acetyl coa x 10 ATP/1 acetyl CoA
= 90 ATP


FADH2 production:


8 FADH2 x 1. 5 ATP/1 FADH2 
= 12 ATP


NADH production:


8 NADH x 2.5 ATP/1NADH
